description.narrative: Ghana's macro-financial risks have risen in part by concerns over precarious fiscal situation in the context of mounting public debt, contingent liabilities, and growth prospects that are susceptible to more variants and waves of the COVID-19 pandemic. Inadequate management of state-owned enterprises (SOEs), particularly in the energy sector, has resulted in chronic operational losses and substantial accumulated debt. The Government has responded to recent trends by reducing expenditure, but the slower pace of recovery affected revenues on all fronts including personal income tax (PAYE), corporation tax, taxes on self-employed, and excise taxes. Reversing these trends requires a significant and rapid structural reform effort, as Ghana faces a growing burden of interest payments on its public debt, which could constrain the country's industrialization and job creation ambitions.Strengthening the credibility of public finances has become more important. Strong Public Financial Management (PFM) systems have become critical to deriving maximum value for money in these times of fiscal constraints. Despite successes in PFM reforms in the past, including the recent World Bank funded projects - Ghana Economic Management Strengthening Project (P152171) and Public Financial Management Reform Project (P151447) - that significantly supported the PFM reforms in Ghana, effective public service delivery is constrained by fiscal fragility and the underlying problem of weak coordination.The current Program – Ghana PFM for Service Delivery Program - is a PforR Program to support the implementation of government-owned PFM reform Strategy (2022-26) in its entirety. It is complemented by an IPF component to support priority Technical Assistance (TA). The Program is aligned with the World Bank's Country Partnership Framework (CPF) for Ghana for fiscal years (FY) 2022-26. It will primarily contribute to strengthen macroeconomic and fiscal management (CPF objective 3.1). It will also contribute to focus area 2 through improved quality of primary health care, improved access to quality education, and improved delivery of basic services.TThe Program Development Objective (PDO) is to improve resource mobilization and allocation, budget execution and accountability. It is expected to contribute to four key result areas to achieve the PDO: (i) Result Area 1: Improve public resource mobilization (ii) Result Area 2: Improve resource allocation consistent with government priorities (iii) Result Area 3: Improve budget execution and accountability to enable better service delivery and (iv) Result Area 4: Strengthen reforms coordination and stimulus for change.The IPF component draws upon lesson learned from other PforR operations and fiduciary assessments, and is based on request from the Government. Specifically, the IPF component will support the following areas:(a) Public Finance Management. The sub-component will (i) ensure quality control of interconnection solutions for PFM systems, and of training/certification modules provided by the MoF; (ii) define and pilot tools to improve management performance, interface with the project evaluation systems, improving accessibility with the financial audit tools; (iii) provide technical support for the supervision of State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs) by the Public Investment and Assets Division (PIAD), and improved financial and operational performance monitoring dashboards, trainings on SOE fiscal risk analysis and SOE multi-year contracting; (iv) define budgeting and expenditure execution and reporting processes for emergency responses (following climate-related disaster but not only) to ensure rapid mobilization of resources and rapid execution; and (v) gender and climate budgeting.(b) Human Resources Management. The sub-component will (i) ensure quality control of Human Resource Management Information System (HRMIS) implementation; (ii) update the HR strategy; (iii) finance pilots for strengthening the skills of healthcare and teaching staff as well as monitoring absenteeism engaging citizens; (iv) define HR return strategies for health care and teaching staff in crisis and post-crisis situations (security, natural disasters, etc.); (v) foster women civil servants careers by analyzing the impact of financial and career-based mobility incentives to remote areas through gender lens to mitigate negative impact on women civil servants; and draft a strategy for women promotion in managerial position in targeted ministries.(c) Change management. The sub-component will finance international and local expertise providing technical guidance and support to the departments leading the targeted reforms, on change management, including but not limited to coaching on Rapid Results Initiatives (RRI).(d) Result Verification. The sub-component will finance the expertise to ensure adequate and independent Disbursement Linked Results (DLR) verification through an Independent Verification Agent (IVA).(e) Program Coordination. The sub-component will finance the required fiduciary, M&E, E&S experts, and other executives as per DLI9 Technical Note to ensure adequate compliance to Bank procedures as well as support the leadership of the MoF in program coordination. It will also support the design and implementation of the GoG program's complaint management mechanism, mid-term and, final evaluations of the Program (including PFM field inspections and PFM research/surveys) and a comprehensive evaluation at the end of the program.
To improve resource mobilization and allocation, budget execution and accountability.

condition.narrative: Section I.A 2 (a) of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement: The Recipient shall maintain throughout implementation of theOperation, a program coordination office (“Program Coordination Office” or “PCO”) with a composition, mandate and resourcessatisfactory to the Association, including: (i) a Program director; (ii) eight (8) Program executives; (iii) a procurementspecialist; (iv) a financial management specialist; (v) an environmental and social management specialist; (vi) a monitoring andevaluation specialist; (vii) eight (8) change management facilitators, all with qualifications, experience and under terms ofreference satisfactory to the Association.Section I.C of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement: The Recipient shall: (1) not laterthan three (3) months after the Effective Date, recruit and thereafter maintain at all times during the implementation of theProgram, an Independent Verification Agent, under terms of reference acceptable to the Association; and (2) ensure that theIndependent Verification Agent prepares and provides verification reports certifying the achievement of the DLRs set out in SectionIV.A.2, in accordance with the Verification Protocol.

title.narrative: Enhanced coordination and alignment of external finance

baseline.value: - Five (5) sectors had 2 meetings of the SWG held to discuss the development and implementation of the respective sector development plans however, annual donor coordination report was not produced - Twenty three (23) donor funded projects on the government budget are using GIFMIS, but it is not sure how many are channeled through the TSA

target.value: -14 sectors where at least 2 sector working group meetings are held: (a) to discuss the development and implementation of the respective sector development plans; and (b) to produce an Annual Donor Coordination Report for a given Fiscal Year- Forty (40) existing and newly signed donor funded projects on the government budget and are spent through the Treasury Single Account (TSA) using GIFMI

actual.value: - Seven (7) sectors had 2 meetings of the SWG held to discuss the development and implementation of the respective sector development plans however, annual donor coordination report was not produced - Thirteen (13) donor funded projects on the government budget and spent through TSA using GIFMIS.

baseline.value: - New Tax Expenditure bill submitted to the Parliament. Current practices are not transparent. - No incentives for climate smart investments currently in place- Non-salaried active taxpayers are total 159,000

target.value: - Adopt data-driven, revised policy framework for conceptualizing, appraising, and approving new tax expenditures by Cabinet, based on the publication of repository of tax expenditures and the cost of these expenditures- 500 tax expenditure claims granted for clmate smart investments- 79,500 increase in the number of non-salaried active taxpayers

actual.value: Tax Exemption Act (Act 1083) was passed in 2022 and administrative guidelines published in August 2023. A tax expenditures repository completed during the last quarter of 2023. The GoG granted 14 tax expenditure claims granted for climate smart investments and tax expenditures on imports for 2023 were published in the 2024 Annual Budget Statement. The GRA added 27,313 non- salaried tax payers to the register and deployed online platforms to allow tax payers to file and pay taxes.
